retrievals.basis: Rowan's own text settles the entry's line-51 characterisation: she 'puts forward the proposal' (her words), argues the Meroitic-Nubian affiliation 'should finally be abandoned', concludes only 'a strong possibility', and explicitly makes 'no claims as to the likeliest individual candidate'. This is a genuine competing argument, not a settled replacement. Her analysis is built on 'the phonemic values of the signs and their distribution' - i.e. it operates on the deciphered sign layer, consistent with the entry's separation of sign values from semantic understanding. Her section 5 states Meroitic and Old Nubian 'show no parity', which independently supports the entry's 'not identity with Old Nubian' leg from the opposite camp to Rilly.

limits: The entry cites [R12, ch. III] for the affiliation statement; chapter III of the 2012 book remains unread, and an open-access summary article by the same author (Ityopis 2011) is not the book chapter - this residual stands and keeps whole-claim support at partial. Rowan's paper is itself a contested proposal (working-papers volume, her analysis rests on consonantal-compatibility isomorphy); nothing here adjudicates the correct classification, and no independent promotion verification is performed. The Ityopis paper's NES framing ('the search for related languages has recently come to an end') is more confident than the entry's 'proposed'/'debated' wording; the entry's conservative calibration is retained because Rowan's competing paper documents that no unanimity exists. Unrestricted translation remains unverified: no Meroitic text was translated in this pass, and the entry's own table (transliteration is not pronunciation; names/titles/formulae are better understood than narratives) is not tested against a fresh edition here. No restricted or pirated texts were used; all retrievals were from the official publisher, journal, or repository (via the Internet Archive capture of the repository file).
